blocks.text: 1.1.3 Complex Numbers as Ordered Pairs of Real Numbers

Is sabaq mein hum complex number ko ek naye libaas mein dekhenge: ordered pair (tarteeb wala jora) \((a, b)\). Pichle sabaq mein aap ne \(a + ib\) ki shakal mein jama, tafreeq aur zarb seekhi thi; ab wahi saare rules pairs ki zubaan mein likhenge. Faida yeh hai ke is tareeqe mein \(\sqrt{-1}\) ko "maan lene" ki zaroorat nahi parti; sab kuch do aam real numbers se ban jata hai, aur aage Argand diagram mein point lagana bhi isi se asaan hoga.

Pehle "ordered pair" ka matlab samajh lein. Ordered pair do numbers ka aisa jora hai jis mein tarteeb (order) ahem hai: \((2, 5)\) aur \((5, 2)\) do alag pairs hain. Jaise ghar ka pata "gali number 2, makan number 5" aur "gali number 5, makan number 2" do alag ghar hain. \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}\) ka matlab hai woh tamam pairs jin ke dono components real numbers hon.
Ab kitab ki definition: maan lijiye \(C\) un ordered pairs ka set hai jo \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}\) se liye gaye hain aur jin par yeh properties lagu hoti hain:

items: \((a, b) = (c, d) \Leftrightarrow a = c \wedge b = d\)

blocks.text: To \(C\) ko complex numbers ka set kehte hain. Yeh dekhna bhi asaan hai ke \[(a, b) - (c, d) = (a - c,\ b - d)\]

items: Agar \(k\) koi bhi real number ho to \(k(a, b) = (ka, kb)\).

blocks.text: Properties (i), (ii) aur (iii) baari baari do complex numbers ki barabari (equality), sum (jama) aur product (zarb) define karti hain, aur un ke baad likha hua rule difference (tafreeq) batata hai. Property (iv) real number aur complex number ka product define karti hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein likha hai ke (i), (ii), (iii) "equality, sum and difference" define karti hain. Lekin (iii) \((a,b)(c,d) = (ac-bd,\ ad+bc)\) to product (zarb) ka rule hai. Difference wala rule \((a,b)-(c,d) = (a-c,\ b-d)\) is ke baad alag likha gaya hai.

Ab in properties ko ek ek kar ke samajhte hain. Property (i) kehti hai ke do pairs tabhi barabar hain jab pehla component pehle ke barabar ho aur doosra doosre ke barabar ho (\(\wedge\) ka matlab "aur"). Sirf ek component barabar ho to kaafi nahi. Property (ii) mein jama component ba component hota hai, bilkul pichle sabaq ke "real ke saath real, imaginary ke saath imaginary" ki tarah. Property (iii) zarb ka rule hai; yeh pehli nazar mein ajeeb lagta hai, lekin asal mein yeh wohi rule hai jo \((a+ib)(c+id)\) kholne se aata hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Pair \((a, b)\) bas \(a + ib\) likhne ka doosra tareeqa hai: pehla component = real part, doosra component = imaginary part. Misaal: \((8, 9)\) ka matlab \(8 + 9i\) aur \((5, -6)\) ka matlab \(5 - 6i\).
Product ka rule (iii) bilkul wohi hai jo 1.1.2 mein tha: \((a+ib)(c+id) = (ac-bd) + i(ad+bc)\). Is liye ise ratne ki zaroorat nahi; agar bhool jayein to pair ko \(a + ib\) mein badal kar zarb kar lijiye.
Ab ek khoobsurat baat dekhiye. Is zubaan mein \(i = (0, 1)\) hai. Rule (iii) lagaiye:
\[(0,1)(0,1) = (0\cdot0 - 1\cdot1,\ 0\cdot1 + 1\cdot0)\]
\[= (-1,\ 0)\]
Aur \((-1, 0)\) real number \(-1\) hai. Yani pairs ki definition se khud ba khud \(i^2 = -1\) nikal aaya, \(\sqrt{-1}\) ko "ijaad" kiye baghair. Is liye yeh definition mathematicians ko zyada pasand hai.
Ab kitab ki pehli misaal hal karte hain. Sab se pehle hum yeh samajhte hain ke sawal mein find kya karna hai, phir given values pehchanenge, phir har hisse ke liye sahi rule chunenge.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.problem: Find the sum, difference and product of the complex numbers \((8, 9)\) and \((5, -6)\).
steps:
Diya gaya (Given): \(z_1 = (8, 9)\) aur \(z_2 = (5, -6)\).
Maloom karna hai (To find): \(z_1 + z_2\), \(z_1 - z_2\) aur \(z_1 z_2\).
Tareeqa (Method): teen kaam hain, aur har ek ka apna rule hai. Sum ke liye rule (ii), difference ke liye \((a,b)-(c,d) = (a-c, b-d)\), aur product ke liye rule (iii) \((a,b)(c,d) = (ac-bd, ad+bc)\). Pehle values pehchan lein: \(a = 8, b = 9, c = 5, d = -6\). Dhyan dein ke \(d\) negative hai; poore sawal mein sab se zyada ghaltiyan isi minus se hoti hain.

Step 1: sum
\[(8, 9) + (5, -6)\]
\[= (8+5,\ 9+(-6))\]
\[= (13,\ 3)\]
Kyun: rule (ii) pehle components ko aapas mein aur doosre components ko aapas mein jama karta hai. \(9 + (-6)\) ka matlab \(9 - 6 = 3\), kyunke negative number jama karna tafreeq karne ke barabar hai.

Step 2: difference
\[(8, 9) - (5, -6)\]
\[= (8-5,\ 9-(-6))\]
\[= (3,\ 9+6)\]
\[= (3,\ 15)\]
Kyun: tafreeq bhi component ba component hoti hai. Pehla component \(8 - 5 = 3\). Doosre mein \(-6\) ko minus karna hai, aur minus ka minus plus hota hai: \(9 - (-6) = 9 + 6 = 15\).
Dhyan dein: kitab is line mein \((5, 15)\) chhapti hai, jo ghalat hai (neeche "Kitab ki ghalti" dekhiye); sahi jawab \((3, 15)\) hai.

Step 3: product ka pehla component \(ac - bd\)
\[8 \cdot 5 - (9)(-6)\]
\[= 40 + 54\]
\[= 94\]
Kyun: rule \((a,b)(c,d) = (ac-bd,\ ad+bc)\) mein pehla component \(ac - bd\) hai. Yahan \(ac = 8 \times 5 = 40\) aur \(bd = 9 \times (-6) = -54\). Ab \(40 - (-54)\) ka matlab \(40 + 54 = 94\). Yahi woh jagah hai jahan \(i^2 = -1\) chupke se kaam kar raha hai.

Step 4: product ka doosra component \(ad + bc\)
\[8(-6) + 9 \cdot 5\]
\[= -48 + 45\]
\[= -3\]
Kyun: doosra component \(ad + bc\) hai: \(ad = 8 \times (-6) = -48\) aur \(bc = 9 \times 5 = 45\). Kitab ise \(9 \cdot 5 + (-6)(8)\) likhti hai; yeh wahi do products ulti tarteeb mein hain, jawab ek hi hai.
\[(8, 9)(5, -6) = (94,\ -3)\]

Tasdeeq (Check):
Ab apna jawab doosre tareeqe se check karte hain. Numbers ko \(8 + 9i\) aur \(5 - 6i\) likh kar aam tareeqe se zarb dein:
\[(8+9i)(5-6i)\]
\[= 40 - 48i + 45i - 54i^2\]
\[= 40 + 54 - 3i\]
\[= 94 - 3i\]
Yeh wahi \((94, -3)\) hai. Difference ko check karne ke liye usay \(z_2\) mein wapas jama karein: \((3, 15) + (5, -6) = (8, 9)\), jo pehla number hi hai. Dono jawab sahi.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein difference \((8-5,\ 9-(-6)) = (5,\ 15)\) chhapa hai. Lekin \(8 - 5 = 3\) hota hai, is liye sahi difference \((3, 15)\) hai. Sum \((13, 3)\) aur product \((94, -3)\) kitab mein sahi hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Is misaal se ek sabaq: product ka rule yaad na rahe to ghabraiye mat. Pair ko \(a + ib\) mein likhiye, brackets kholiye, \(i^2 = -1\) lagaiye, aur wapas pair bana lijiye. Imtihan mein pehle rule se hal kijiye, phir yeh tareeqa check ke liye istemaal kijiye.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \((a, b) \leftrightarrow a + ib\): pehla component real part, doosra imaginary part.
2. Do pairs tabhi barabar hain jab dono components barabar hon.
3. Sum aur difference component ba component hote hain.
4. Product: \((a,b)(c,d) = (ac-bd,\ ad+bc)\); real multiple: \(k(a,b) = (ka, kb)\).
5. \((0, 1)(0, 1) = (-1, 0)\), yani pairs ki zubaan mein bhi \(i^2 = -1\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
Zarb ko bhi component ba component kar dena: \((a,b)(c,d) \ne (ac, bd)\). Misaal: \((0,1)(0,1)\) ka jawab \((-1, 0)\) hai, \((0, 1)\) nahi.
Negative components ke sath sign ki ghalti: \(9 - (-6) = 15\) hai, aur \(-(9)(-6) = +54\). Har minus ko bracket mein likh kar chaliye.
Pair ki tarteeb ulat dena: \((5, -6)\) ka matlab \(5 - 6i\) hai, \(-6 + 5i\) nahi.
